insight.title: The Statistician Who Armored the Undamaged Parts of Planes
insight.subtitle: How a counterintuitive decision during WWII saved thousands of pilots.
insight.notificationHook: He armored the parts without bullet holes

sections.text: During World War II, the military wanted to armor returning bombers. They analyzed the bullet holes on surviving aircraft, planning to reinforce the most heavily damaged areas.
But statistician Abraham Wald disagreed. He ordered the mechanics to armor the completely untouched areas instead, defying the obvious data presented right in front of them.
Wald realized the surviving planes only showed where a bomber could be hit and still fly. The planes hit in the clean areas had all crashed at sea.
The most critical lessons are often hidden in what didn't happen.
